title: Specified inverse-image comparison is the completion unit
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below have $\ell$ invertible and use small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For each scheme $W$, set $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_W$ of $B_{W,n}$-modules with quotient-linear transitions, and its unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $\mathcal R_W$ for simultaneous derived reduction, $U_W$ for exact restriction to $\widehat R_W$-module towers and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim U_W$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $G=g^{-1}$ on completed module complexes, transporting scalars through $g^{-1}\widehat R_Y\cong\widehat R_X$ [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Write $P_g=Lg^*$ for completed integral pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] and let $\kappa^g_N:GN\to P_gN$ be the SPECIFIED map of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b). For any ambient complex $N\in D(\widehat R_Y)$ define $\widehat N=\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YN$ and let $u_N:N\to\widehat N$ be the actual unit of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\theta_{g,N}:P_gN\xrightarrow{\sim}G\widehat N$$
such that
$$\theta_{g,N}\circ\kappa^g_N=G(u_N).$$
Here $\theta$ is the map of entire strict quotient cones induced by multiplication $g^*Q_n\to GQ_n$, $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, and the product/cone comparison for the exact site equivalence, for one flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to N$. The displayed equation specifies the zero shifted-coordinate cone map, not only its projections. It is independent of $Q$ under the canonical resolution comparisons and natural for derived morphisms. In particular, if $N$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], then this specified $\kappa^g_N$ is invertible, with inverse $G(u_N)^{-1}\theta_{g,N}$. No invertibility is asserted for incomplete ambient objects, and no equality with an unspecified choice of the isomorphism $\lambda_N$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose $q:Q\to N$ flat-term K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; for the formula of step 3 take the resolution with which $P_gN$ is formed in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] (b), other choices being compared in step 2. Set $Q_n=Q\otimes B_{Y,n}$, $r_n(z)=z\otimes1$, $D=U_Y(Q_n)_n$ and $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*Q_n$ with its strict transitions. By [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model], the normalized quotient cone $H(D)$ realizes $\widehat N$ and its augmentation $v_Q(z)=(0,(r_nz)_n)$ represents the actual $u_N$ after $[q]^{-1}$. This fixes the entire cone map.

source.place: Clauses (2)-(3); assembly after the Q26 re-split, step 1

proof.text: By [lem-trf-isomorphism-multiplication-cone-descent], $j_n(x\otimes a)=ax$ gives $j:C\simeq GD$, with inverse $i_n(x)=x\otimes1$, and $\eta_D:GH(D)\simeq H(GD)$ is the product comparison on both coordinates. Set $\theta=\eta_D^{-1}H(j)$. The same lemma identifies its source with $P_gN$ and gives its naturality for all derived morphisms and independence under the canonical resolution comparisons. All hypotheses hold: $g$ is a scheme isomorphism, the sites are small and coefficients and quotient transitions are the specified ones.

source.place: Clauses (2)-(3); assembly after the Q26 re-split, step 2

proof.text: By [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] (b), $\kappa^g_N$ is represented on $GQ$ by $w\mapsto(0,(i_nG(r_n)w)_n)$, then $[Gq]^{-1}$. Multiplication cancels each $i_n$ ($j_ni_n=\mathrm{id}$), so $H(j)$ sends this chain map to $w\mapsto(0,(G(r_n)w)_n)$. The latter is exactly $\eta_DG(v_Q)$: by [lem-trf-isomorphism-multiplication-cone-descent] $\eta_D$ is $\phi_D$ on both coordinates, so the shifted coordinate stays zero and the unshifted product has components $\mathrm{pr}_n\phi_DG((r_n)_n)=G(r_n)$. Applying $\eta_D^{-1}$ gives $G(v_Q)$ as an actual chain map. Hence, by [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model] and functoriality of the exact $G$, $\theta\kappa^g_N=G([v_Q][q]^{-1})=G(u_N)$. This checks both coordinates. Since $\kappa=\theta^{-1}G(u)$ and the adjunction unit of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] is natural, this equality also gives naturality and resolution independence of the specified $\kappa$.

source.place: Clauses (2)-(3); assembly after the Q26 re-split, step 3

proof.text: For derived-complete $N$, apply [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] with $L=E$. Its canonical completion map is invertible and is represented, after $N\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}\widehat R_Y\simeq N$, by $v_Q$. By [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model] this is the actual $u_N$. Consequently $G(u_N)$ is invertible, and $G(u_N)^{-1}\theta$ is a two-sided inverse of $\kappa^g_N=\theta^{-1}G(u_N)$ by cancellation. Completeness is used only here; the ambient normalization makes no invertibility claim for incomplete $N$.
